notes: Trigger + behaviour evals. The behaviour ones exist because the failure modes here are claims, not crashes: a per-agent robots rule read as a site-wide block, a lab Lighthouse score presented as a field verdict, schema sold as a ranking lever, or an indexation number invented because Search Console is missing. Run with skill-creator's harness at --num-workers 2 (the harness is unreliable under higher concurrency and silently scores failed invocations as 'not triggered').

evals.name: robots-per-agent-not-sitewide
evals.prompt:
Here's my robots.txt, can you check it over?

User-agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: *?lightbox=

# Block PetalBot
User-agent: PetalBot
Disallow: /

Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
evals.expected_output: Correctly reads the Disallow: / as scoped to PetalBot only, does NOT report the site as blocked to all crawlers, and notes the missing AI crawler policy as a decision rather than a defect.
assertions: Does NOT claim the site blocks all crawlers or that Googlebot is blocked
Explicitly attributes the Disallow: / to PetalBot
Notes the sitemap directive is present
Raises the AI crawler policy (GPTBot/ClaudeBot/OAI-SearchBot etc.) as undeclared
Frames the AI policy as a business decision, not a failure

evals.name: indexation-without-search-console
evals.prompt: Can you tell me what percentage of my site's pages Google has actually indexed? The site is https://example.com
evals.expected_output: Says this is not measurable without Search Console, explains that a crawl reports what the crawler fetched rather than what Google stored, and gives the manual route (Search Console -> Pages, plus the Crawled-not-indexed vs Discovered-not-indexed split).
assertions: Does NOT invent or estimate an indexation percentage
States that Search Console is the only source for this and is not connected
Distinguishes what a crawler can see from what Google indexed
Names the Search Console Pages report as the manual route
Mentions the 85% indexed-to-submitted healthy benchmark OR the Crawled/Discovered-not-indexed distinction

evals.name: schema-is-not-a-ranking-lever
evals.prompt: I read that adding schema markup gets you 3x more citations in ChatGPT and helps you rank. Worth doing on my site?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back with the evidence conflict: the multiplier claims are correlational and from schema-tool vendors, Ahrefs (1,885 pages) and SearchAtlas found no causal uplift, and Google has confirmed structured data is not a direct ranking factor. Recommends it anyway for rich-result eligibility and entity clarity.
assertions: Does NOT endorse the 3x citation claim as established
Names the counter-evidence (Ahrefs and/or SearchAtlas found no uplift)
States Google has confirmed structured data is not a direct ranking factor
Notes the vendor claims are correlational and self-interested
Still recommends schema, but for rich results and entity disambiguation

evals.name: lighthouse-100-but-failing
evals.prompt: My PageSpeed score is 100 on mobile but my rankings haven't moved. What's going on with my Core Web Vitals?
evals.expected_output: Explains the lab-versus-field distinction: a 100 Lighthouse score is a simulation and Google ranks on CrUX field data at p75 over 28 days, so the page can score 100 and still fail. Also frames CWV as a floor, not a lever, so passing buys nothing further.
assertions: Distinguishes lab (Lighthouse) from field (CrUX) data
States Google ranks on field data only
Mentions the 75th percentile and/or the 28-day rolling window
States Core Web Vitals are a floor/tiebreaker, not a ranking lever
Does NOT recommend further speed optimization for ranking reasons if already passing

evals.name: csr-site-invisible-to-ai
evals.prompt: We built the site in React with client-side rendering. Google seems to index us fine and rankings are okay. Any technical SEO concern there?
evals.expected_output: Yes: Google renders in a second wave 24-72 hours later, but GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot frequently do not execute JavaScript at all, so the site can rank normally in Google and be absent from AI answers. Recommends the disable-JavaScript test and server-rendering the content, links and especially metadata.
assertions: Explains Google's two-wave indexing with the 24-72 hour delay
States that AI crawlers frequently do not execute JavaScript at all
Makes the point that Google rankings looking fine does not rule this out
Recommends a concrete diagnostic (disable JavaScript and reload, or compare raw vs rendered HTML)
Recommends server-rendering content/links/metadata rather than a full rebuild

evals.name: disallow-plus-noindex-conflict
evals.prompt: I want these thank-you pages out of Google. I've added noindex to them and also blocked /thank-you/ in robots.txt to be thorough. Good?
evals.expected_output: No: disallowed means Google never fetches the page, so it never reads the noindex, and if the URL is linked anywhere it can stay indexed as a bare URL indefinitely. Tell them to pick one - allow crawling and keep the noindex.
assertions: Identifies the combination as broken, not thorough
Explains that a disallowed page is never fetched so the noindex is never read
Notes the URL can remain indexed as a bare URL with no description
Recommends removing the Disallow and keeping noindex (allow crawling)

evals.name: hreflang-not-needed
evals.prompt: We sell to the US, UK and Australia from one English website. Should we set up hreflang?
evals.expected_output: Almost certainly not: one English site with no meaningful differences does not need hreflang, and implementing it adds permanent maintenance for no benefit. Recommends recording the decision as a documented not-applicable so nobody implements it later.
assertions: Recommends against implementing hreflang for this case
Explains it is only needed with substantially different content per language or market
Notes that implementing it unnecessarily adds maintenance for no benefit
Suggests documenting the not-applicable decision rather than leaving it blank
Does NOT claim hreflang would improve rankings

evals.name: tier-order-over-easy-wins
evals.prompt: Technical audit came back with: no Organization schema, no breadcrumbs, LCP at 3.1s on the blog template, sitemap contains 40 URLs that 404, and robots.txt returns a 500. What should we fix first?
evals.expected_output: robots.txt 500 first - it stops Googlebot crawling the entire site. Then the sitemap 404s. Schema and speed last, because fixing schema on a site that cannot be crawled is polishing something invisible.
assertions: Puts the robots.txt 5xx first
Explains a 5xx on robots.txt stops Googlebot crawling the whole site
Puts the sitemap 404s ahead of schema and speed
Puts schema last or near-last
Articulates the tier principle: a lower-layer failure invalidates work above it

evals.name: faq-schema-retired-but-keep-it
evals.prompt: Google killed FAQ rich results. Should I strip the FAQPage schema off my 60 pages?
evals.expected_output: No: the Google rich result sunset on 7 May 2026, but ChatGPT, Perplexity and Bing Copilot still consume FAQPage markup. Leave it, just stop expecting Google output.
assertions: Recommends leaving the markup in place
Confirms the Google rich result is retired
States that non-Google engines (ChatGPT/Perplexity/Bing Copilot) still use it
Reframes the expectation rather than the markup

evals.name: full-audit-triggers-crawl-first
evals.prompt: Run a full technical SEO audit on https://example.com
evals.expected_output: Invokes the skill, crawls once with crawl.py, then runs technical.py / schema.py / vitals.py / render_diff.py off that one graph, and reports in tier order with Search Console named as not connected.
assertions: Uses scripts/crawl.py first rather than fetching pages ad hoc
Runs the check scripts against the crawl graph rather than re-fetching
Reports findings grouped or ordered by the tier pyramid
Names Search Console as not connected rather than approximating indexation
Does not present more than about five top-priority findings

evals.name: build-mode-artifacts
evals.prompt: Generate me a corrected robots.txt and a clean sitemap for https://example.com based on what's actually wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: Runs emit.py (BUILD mode), produces the files, and reports what changed and why. Does not deploy anything.
assertions: Uses scripts/emit.py rather than hand-writing the files
The generated robots.txt contains a Sitemap: directive
The generated robots.txt declares an AI crawler policy without the deprecated anthropic-ai agent
Explains each change rather than silently applying it
States that nothing was deployed

evals.name: does-not-poach-onpage
evals.prompt: My title tags are all too long and my blog posts don't have enough internal links. Can you fix the on-page stuff?
evals.expected_output: Hands off to seo-onpage rather than answering from this skill. Title tags, content and internal linking are Tier 2.
assertions: Routes the request to seo-onpage
Does NOT run the technical crawl scripts for this
Correctly identifies titles and internal linking as on-page/Tier 2, not technical/Tier 3
